explanation: A people who lived east of the Jordan River, often in conflict with Israel.
King of the Ammonites, son of Nahash, who insulted David's envoys.
The second king of Israel, a central figure in the Old Testament.
David's military commander and nephew, played an important role in many of David's military campaigns.
A country northeast of Israel, allied with the Ammonites against David and his army.
Joab's brother and one of David's most powerful warriors, helped lead Israel's army against the Ammonites and Syrians.
Former king of the Ammonites, father of Hanun, had a good relationship with David before his death.
An organized military force consisting of soldiers and officers who fight for a nation or a leader.
